Experiment protocol: Paper rotor
Make a small paper rotor from a 3-by-12-centimeter strip: slit the top six centimeters down its center and bend the two resulting blades in opposite directions. Fold the lower end upward twice for stiffness. Drop from shoulder height over a clear floor and observe rotation. Adjust blade length on a second model while keeping paper and release height constant.
provenance: NASA/JPL-Caltech Education, Make a Paper Mars Helicopter; https://www.jpl.nasa.gov/edu/resources/project/make-a-paper-mars-helicopter-2/ . Original small paper-model adaptation; dimensions and controlled-trial wording are editorial choices.

Experiment protocol: Rotor direction
Make two identical paper rotors with split upper blades bent in opposite directions and folded lower bodies. Reverse the blade folds on just one rotor. Drop each from the same shoulder height, filming if useful, and compare rotation direction. Keep the observer’s viewpoint fixed: clockwise from above is counterclockwise from below.
provenance: NASA/JPL-Caltech Education, Make a Paper Mars Helicopter; https://www.jpl.nasa.gov/edu/resources/project/make-a-paper-mars-helicopter-2/ . Original small paper-model adaptation; dimensions and controlled-trial wording are editorial choices.
